Upgrading a strfry relay from 1.1.2 to 1.1.3 removes a double-free guard rather than adding one.

The tag, dated 4 September 2026, contains two commits and touches two paths: CHANGES and the golpe submodule pointer. No strfry source file changes. golpe moves from 72477956 to 73ba63b5, which moves external/uWebSockets from 1ef91686 to 45816de8. That commit is titled Revert "Prevent duplicate teardown from stale epoll events".

What comes out are two short hunks merged in July as uWebSockets pull request #6: a skip for closed polls in the epoll dispatch loop, and an early return at the top of WebSocket::onEnd. Their own comments explain the case. closeSocket() sets the fd to -1 but defers deleting the object, so a stale event in the same epoll batch re-enters onEnd, fires disconnectionHandler twice and double-frees both the user data and the WebSocket. The guard shipped in 1.1.1 and 1.1.2.

The headline fix of 1.1.2 is not affected. 45816de8 sits on top of the fragment buffer check, not against it.

We read the pointers rather than the version numbers, because on this release the version number tells you nothing. The single changelog line is the only statement about any of it in the artifacts.

If you run strfry, do you know which uWebSockets commit your last build resolved?
